testCases.title: Notification Templates List — HTTP 500 (orphaned TwitterNotificationEntity discriminator)
testCases.failedAssertion: [GRID] at least 3 built-in notification template types present; API GET /api/notification/templates?take=20 returns non-empty array
testCases.notes: POST /api/notifications (the templates list query used by the admin 'Notification list' blade) returns HTTP 500: 'Unable to materialize entity instance of type NotificationEntity. No discriminators matched the discriminator value TwitterNotificationEntity.' Angular logs unhandled rejection; grid renders column headers but zero data rows. Root cause: orphaned TwitterNotificationEntity rows (removed/disabled Twitter notification type) break the EF Core discriminator query for the entire list. Individual templates still load via GET /api/notifications/<type>. Severity: High — entire notification templates list is unusable in Admin SPA.
consoleErrors: Unhandled rejection: POST /api/notifications → 500 Internal Server Error

testCases.title: Member Invitation List — Empty response body
testCases.failedAssertion: [BODY] response has totalCount >= 0 and results array
testCases.notes: GET /api/members/invitations?take=5 → 200 but with completely empty body (content-length 0, no content-type). No totalCount or results structure returned. This is a contract violation — the endpoint should return at least {totalCount:0, results:[]} for an empty collection.
POST /api/pricing/pricelists/import {} → 405 Method Not Allowed (not 500, no stack trace). Pricing blade accessible after. Safety invariant holds.

testCases.title: Bulk Delete Without Auth — Returns 302 redirect instead of 401
testCases.failedAssertion: [STATUS] DELETE returns 401 Unauthorized; [HEADER] WWW-Authenticate header present
testCases.notes: All 3 unauthenticated DELETEs return HTTP 302 redirect to /?ReturnUrl=... (cookie-auth challenge), not 401 + WWW-Authenticate. Access is correctly denied (no data deleted), so this is not a security bypass. However the API contract assertion (401 + WWW-Authenticate) fails. Note: when X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest header is included (as the SPA always sends), endpoints return 401 correctly.

testCases.title: User Lockout Configuration — Lockout settings not in platform settings API
testCases.failedAssertion: [BODY] settings array contains lockout-related entries (MaxPasswordAge, MaxFailedAccessAttempts)
testCases.notes: GET /api/platform/settings?keyword=lockout → 200 but keyword filter is ignored (returns all 301 settings). No lockout/MaxFailedAccessAttempts/MaxPasswordAge entries exist in the module settings store — these are ASP.NET Identity configuration options, not VC module settings. The assertion is based on an incorrect assumption about where lockout config lives.

testCases.title: Category Hierarchy Depth Check — Wrong REST endpoint for paged category listing
testCases.failedAssertion: [BODY] response contains categories with id/name/parentCategoryId; at least 1 category with non-null parentCategoryId
testCases.notes: GET /api/catalog/categories?take=20&deepSearch=true → 200 with empty array (endpoint requires ids[] parameter, not paging). Category hierarchy IS healthy: GraphQL categories query returns 445 categories with parent{} structure (verified). Root cause: case uses the wrong REST endpoint. Correct endpoint for paged category listing is POST /api/catalog/categories/search.

bugs.title: Notification Templates List broken — HTTP 500 on POST /api/notifications (orphaned TwitterNotificationEntity discriminator)
bugs.description: POST /api/notifications (the list query used by Admin SPA Notification list blade) returns HTTP 500: 'Unable to materialize entity instance of type NotificationEntity. No discriminators matched the discriminator value TwitterNotificationEntity.' The entire notification templates list is unusable in Admin SPA. Individual templates still load via GET /api/notifications/<type>. Root cause: orphaned TwitterNotificationEntity rows remain in DB after the Twitter notification type was removed/disabled, and EF Core no longer has that discriminator registered.
